- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.6), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70.5), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 1–2% for the following 5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the 10–15 day horizon; apply +0.5 to +1.5% bias to longer-term forecasts (especially 20+ days).
- When sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often lags; add 1–2 days of lagged momentum to forecast if price >70.
- Model frequently underestimates the “mean reversion” phase after a spike; if sentiment turns neutral or slightly negative, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to account for rebound.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be 0.5–1.5% below true outcome; apply +0.75% bias to 30d forecasts unless sentiment is strongly negative.
